(a) a new framework is presented for understanding the SFQ-based algorithm; and (b) a statistical study of wavelet coefficients verifies that the SFQ-based code is designed around a zero-tree data structure, and suggests the design of alternative data structures.

(i) the SFQ-based wavelet image coder can be viewed as an on-line, image-adaptive, entropy-constrained vector-quantizer; and (ii) the performance gain of this coder over conventional wavelet image coders is due to its being designed with a more accurate characterization of the joint probability distributions of wavelet coefficients in mind, namely, the one that is used by the zero-tree data-structure.

the SFQ-based algorithm is a simplified attempt to implement a global ECVQ with an image-sized codevector dimension and an image-adaptive application; that the SFQ coder is designed around one conveniently efficient collection of sets of wavelet coefficient vectors, namely, the sets of coefficients in zero-tree structures; and that improved performance is possible by designing data structures that more accurately characterize the joint probabilities of wavelet coefficients in high-frequency bands.

the development of a new framework for the design of efficient wavelet image coders.

the development of a new class of image coders based on the wavelet decomposition of an image, which exploit dependencies between wavelet coefficients using a novel data structure, the "zero-tree" structure.
the development of new image compression algorithms that are based on wavelet decompositions and exploit the dependencies between the wavelet coefficients in the hierarchical tree structure.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the SFQ-based and related image coding algorithms can be understood as a simplified attempt at designing an entropy-constrained image coder, and that the performance gain achieved by these algorithms can be attributed to the use of the zero-tree data-structure, which is an efficient representation of the joint probability distribution of arbitrary sets of high-frequency wavelet coefficients.

the new class of image coding algorithms based on zero-tree structures are, in fact, simplified attempts to exploit the joint statistics of wavelet coefficients in an entropy-constrained vector-quantization (ECVQ)-type framework, but using the zero-tree data structures as the sets of coefficients over which the ECVQ framework is applied.
